decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through-glass vias build on Plan Optik's core structured-wafer competence and serve MEMS and advanced packaging demand, which was rising after 2020, so performance is likely near aspiration and the product costs little to keep in the portfolio.
Carrier wafers are a simple, low-cost extension of the standard glass wafer business with steady recurring demand, so there is no shortfall that would trigger problemistic search.

The copper interposer is a newer and more uncertain technology, but its prominent SEMICON launch and the strong semiconductor cycle give the firm enough slack and strategic reason to keep developing it rather than cut it early.

The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand mainly sells existing standard products through an extra channel, so it is cheap to maintain, although it could be folded back into the main brand if online sales stay below aspiration.

Glass-based circuit boards are the most speculative product and further from the core business, but in a booming market with available slack a small specialist firm is likely to keep the option open for another year.
